messages:
Mina: hey all, new hire here (Mina). trying to follow the onboarding checklist and hit a failure on our Buildkite pipeline when it tries to fetch secrets from GitHub Actions secrets store via the org app. pipeline: redwood/onboarding-ci, step: publish-images. anyone run into GH Actions -> Buildkite secrets bridge issues?
arjun: welcome Mina! quick question: is the pipeline using the github-app token exchange or a repo PAT stored in org secrets?
Mina: it should be using the github-app exchange. log shows a 403 when the exchange service calls the GH API: 
```
HTTP 403: Forbidden - resource not accessible by integration
endpoint: POST https://api.github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/package/registry/permissions
```
ci-bot: Buildkite: build #3 failed — https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding-ci/builds/3
Lena: that error means the GH App doesn't have access to that resource. either missing org-level permission or the app isn't installed on the repo that owns the secret namespace. new joiners often bump into this because we recently migrated some repos under a new org team.
arjun: action items to try: 1) confirm the GH App (redwood-ci-app) is installed on the repo/org; 2) check the app's org permissions include 'Secrets: read' (or the minimal required scope for packages/secrets); 3) confirm the pipeline's service account has been added to the 'ci-onboarding' team.
Mina: my GH username is mina-park. can someone check installs?
Lena: @arjun i'll check installs. @Mina i see the app is installed on the org but not on the repo where the secrets live (infra-config). That explains 403.
ops-bot: Note: GitHub App redwood-ci-app installation changed by Maureen at 2025-08-21T09:02:11Z
arjun: ok i installed the app on infra-config and granted Secrets read for that repo. also added mina-park to ci-onboarding team.
ci-bot: Buildkite: build #4 started — https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding-ci/builds/4
ci-bot: Buildkite: build #4 failed — publish-images step failed, see log: 
```
Error: unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized
Caused by: token exchange returned 403 from GH API
```
Mina: still failing, hmm.
Lena: two more checks — the app needs org-level permission to read action secrets if secrets are at org scope, and the exchange service needs the right audience in its JWT. arjun, can you check the jwt config on the exchange?
arjun: confirmed JWT audience was wrong (leftover from staging). fixed it and re-triggered the exchange.
ci-bot: Buildkite: build #5 started — https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding-ci/builds/5
ci-bot: Buildkite: build #5 passed — all steps green 🎉
Mina: it passed! huge thanks. any docs I should read so I don't block others later?
Lena: i'll drop a short blurb in the onboarding doc: include checklist for GH App installs (repo vs org), required app scopes (Secrets read, Packages write where applicable), and the JWT audience for our token-exchange service. also add a troubleshooting checklist: paste the build link, copy the exact exchange error, include GH username and repo name.
arjun: and ping #eng-infra when you hit this. we can usually fix installs quickly.
Mina: awesome, thanks everyone :grinning:
